The core mechanism operates through an associative memory base (AMB) encoding player performance data. Kolmogorov complexity underpins similarity computation across players, enabling relational inference. This is formalized as a kernel-based similarity measure K(xi, xj), where xi, xj represent performance vectors. The injury prediction model uses this similarity to compute a logistic regression-like probability P(I_t | D_t, S_sim), incorporating weights w_i and similarity factors f(S_i). Accuracy assessment follows standard binary classification metrics, particularly focusing on TPR/FPR trade-offs. These primitives form a closed-loop system: AMB → Similarity Kernel → Injury Model → Report Generation → Validation → Feedback Loop. Failure modes arise from data entropy, insufficient training, or temporal misalignment in validation.
